name: Designers & architects
heading: Your specification. Considered down to the last return.
description: Wallcovering installation and coordination for interior designers and architects: material references, elevations, panel layout and preparation.
intro: Bring the material, elevations and design intent together before installation begins. Pattern placement, natural panel variation and the junctions with joinery all deserve a decision before the first length is cut.

sections.title: Protect the design intent
sections.text: Send the material codes and colourways, along with elevations where the pattern or scene needs a particular position. Mark the focal point and any finish detail that matters to the room.

sections.title: Resolve the material questions early
sections.text: Confirm what has been sampled, what remains provisional and who supplies the material. An agreed sample area can help settle panel layout and appearance before the work is repeated.

sections.title: Connect the drawing to the wall
sections.text: Preparation, finished dimensions and the sequence of adjoining work affect the installation. Include what is known about the substrate, joinery and lighting, and identify anything still to be confirmed.

checklist: Product codes, colourways and sample status
Focal points, panel expectations and junction details

name: Developers & main contractors
heading: Wallcovering packages planned around the site.
description: Plan a wallcovering package with scope, drawing revisions, wall readiness, supply responsibilities, programme and handover.
intro: A reliable package starts with the scope and the sequence. Bring drawings, material delivery and wall readiness into the same conversation before booking the installation across rooms or floors.

sections.title: Define the package
sections.text: Identify the rooms and areas, material references, drawing revisions and supply responsibilities. Include preparation and access in the scope so quotations can be compared on the same basis.

sections.title: Coordinate the programme
sections.text: Show target dates and the work that must finish first. Record who checks wall readiness, how changes are approved and how completed walls will be protected from following trades.

sections.title: Agree the handover
sections.text: Set out any sample-area approval, snagging and documentation requirements. Product performance needs the exact supporting documents and acceptance by the responsible project professional.

checklist: Programme, access rules and tender deadline
Sample approval, protection and handover requirements

name: Hotels & operators
heading: Considered finishes. A programme that respects the building.
description: Wallcovering works for hotels and occupied interiors, with phasing, access, cleaning requirements and maintenance considered together.
intro: A guest room, a corridor and a reception area have different demands. Plan the finish around how each space is used, how it is maintained and when it can be released for work.
downloadLabel: Download a room and phase schedule

sections.title: Plan around occupation
sections.text: Identify which rooms can be released together, permitted working hours and the routes used for deliveries. Include guest access, protection and daily handover expectations.

sections.title: Choose for the actual use
sections.text: Agree appearance and maintenance requirements together. Confirm the exact cleaning instructions and the project performance documents for each proposed product.

sections.title: Keep a usable record
sections.text: A room-by-room record of the installed product, batch and care information helps future maintenance. Discuss spare material and the limits of matching a later repair before handover.

checklist: Room types, floor/phase schedule and occupancy
Working hours, deliveries and access limits
Handover, spare material and maintenance priorities
